cs.t: having reread your comment, i see where you linked to a package on github that appears to have fixed it for you. It seems like implementing a fancontrol tool, and perhaps making a one line edit to /etc/udev/rules.d/60-fan-control.rules so that the tool presets the content as a rule for udevadm to  make it controllable for users without sudo. That seems like it might work for your system, maybe for many laptops with similar firmware. This 'closure' instead of engaging with the potential solution might not feel fun when you're proposing a band-aid. However, instead of directing your conversation to the firmware developer, the comment used system76's github repository to directly speak to system76 customers, and try to shame the one developer  into 'being motivated' So, I can see the reasoning behind the closure as it has gone off the topic of reporting a bug, does not add details useful for improving development toward a fix of the bug, and proposes an assumed solution which would potentially add more noise to later responses from other users who attempted that solution whom it didn't help which has the potential to add more noise to the diagnostics process for this particular bug. As you say, not a firmaware expert, and i understand the frustration at the lack of explanation from system76 in 'Hidden as off-topic' for your comment, but it's not deleted, anyone who want to read it can click the 'expand' button and read it. cs.t: Very sad news.  Crucial Micron is (soon "was") an great brand for computer assembly and upgrade. It is sad to see the brand rushing to the "easy money" stream. This won't be forgotten when the current bubble will evenually  pop  and they might meet the same fate as the now forgotten Elpida (who bought Qimonda wich also failed). The MX500 1st gen (fw M3CR023) was the second best SATA SSD range with the kings the Samsung 860 Evo and Pro. P3 and P3+ were very good drives with great princing for some time, not comparable to the Samsung 970 Evo and Evo+ though. Never had a failure on about 500 units of crucial MX300/500/P1/P3/P3+/P5. Always updated their firmwares, though. Comparatively, had lot of sluggish controllers on Sandisk/WD green/blue SATA SSD, and some BX500. But a lot better than any entry level generic Phison S3111 based SSD. Also very few failures with DDR3/4 DIMMs and SODIMMs. Less than with Kinston and Corsair modules. About the same as Samsung OEM modules from HP/Dell. Now let's just hope Samsung will not follow in their tracks. I don't see WD-Sandisk going corporate only since they do not make DRAMs modules.
cs.th: Micron Announces Exit from Crucial Consumer Business
